findings.question: the fix — is the ko field now decoded per the artifact2 contract at every vb_closure site?
findings.verdict: fixed — two sites corrected, one already-correct site unified through the helper
findings.claim: The contract (src/artifact2.zig:70-76, WZO2 §2.2) puts ko at bits 2..(1+ko_bits): ko = (kb>>2)&((1<<ko_bits)-1). ca1ForwardClosure (:467) and ca2BackwardClosure (:794) decoded with kb>>1, which leaks the side bit (bit 1) into the ko field; the 4×4 sample test (:1013) already used kb>>2. The fix adds keyByteKo (contract decode) and routes all three sites through it, so the whole file has one decode.

RED: 'expected 3, found 6'. GREEN: all 3 key_byte tests pass.

findings.question: the corrected C-A2 figures do NOT match T380's corrected run (98,999,934 / 133,102) — is this two independent correct decoders disagreeing?
findings.verdict: no — the two instruments compute different reachable sets by definition; T380's reachAnalyze skips expanding settled positions (R.is_settled), a restriction the kernel successor relation does not have. Two genuinely independent correct decoders of the kernel closure AGREE on 99,133,034.
findings.claim: The brief's stop-and-report trigger assumes 'two independent correct decoders disagreeing'. Investigation shows T380 could not have re-run vb_closure (its scope was additive-only): its D042-2a figures came from t380_ko_slot.zig reach mode, which skips expansion of settled positions ('if (passes >= 2 or R.is_settled(&pos)) continue;'). The kernel successor relation (rules.legalMoves/applyMove) has no settled check — only passes>=2 is terminal — so children of settled positions are reachable under the closure's definition but absent from T380's. An independent re-implementation of the kernel closure (own visited bitset, own decode, own sweep) agrees with the production path exactly: 99,133,034 reachable, 0 not-in-table, 32 sweeps, and enumerates the 2 non-reachable entries (colex=0 side=-1 ko=16 passes=0 — White to move on the empty board; colex=0 side=1 ko=16 passes=1 — Black to move after a White pass on the empty board). The same independent BFS with T380's settled-skip reproduces T380's published figures exactly (98,999,934 / 133,102 / not_in_table=0), proving the discrepancy is the settled-skip, not the decode. T380's D042-2a characterisation survives with the corrected definition intact: non-reachable ko-set = 0 (both non-reachable entries are ko=NONE).
findings.measurement: probe output: 'PROD: reachable_non_terminal=99133034 reachable_terminal=48505261 not_in_table=0 sweeps=32 status=pass' ; 'IND : reachable=99133034 not_in_table=0 sweeps=32' ; 'non-reachable: colex=0 side=-1 ko=16 passes=0' ; 'non-reachable: colex=0 side=1 ko=16 passes=1' ; 'IND : non_reachable=2' ; 'IND2: settled-skip reachable=98999934 not_in_table=0 sweeps=32 non_reachable=133102'. All four assert-checks pass (production==independent; 0 not-in-table both; non_reachable==2; settled-skip==98,999,934).

findings.question: regression — will the next shift change break a test instead of a denominator?
findings.verdict: yes — new test decodes known keys through the production path
findings.claim: test 'key_byte: ko field decodes at bits 2..(1+ko_bits) — regression for T383 F-7' encodes (side,ko,passes) with the file's own encodeKeyByte and asserts keyByteKo (the production decode used by ca1/ca2 and the sample/full closure tests) recovers the ko field, for ko_bits=5 (4×4, ko=3 and ko=NONE=16 with side=1) and ko_bits=3 (2×2, ko=4). A future shift change (>>1 or otherwise) fails this test at build time.

notes: Discrepancy reporting (brief bar 3): the re-run figures do NOT match T380's corrected run, so this row stops and reports — but the diagnosis in F-4 shows it is not the brief's feared case of two correct decoders disagreeing: the corrected kernel closure is confirmed by two independent correct decoders (99,133,034 / 2 non-reachable), and T380's figure is a different reachability definition (settled-skip), reproduced exactly by the independent BFS with that skip.
